description: We're doing the Health Monitoring System challenge to improve our skills as Applied AI students.
summary:
Team HackBros created an AI-Assisted astronaut health-monitoring system designed for a simulated transit to Mars. The end-to-end platform combines a synthetic multi-astronaut telemetry pipeline, a hybrid anomaly detection engine (using personalized baselines, direction-adjusted Z-scores, rolling drift analysis, and an Isolation Forest), a NASA-referenced explainability module, a FastAPI backend, and an interactive React dashboard.
Our project directly addresses the challenge of maintaining crew health with the constraints of limited or delayed deep space communications. The system establishes individual physiological and behavioral baselines over the first 14 mission days, to detect subtle deviations early. It communicates in a clear, non-diagnostic manner, following the guide of the NASA Human Research Program, and recommends immediate on-board actions as opposed waiting for delayed responses from Earth. 
This capability is vital for future space exploration, where communication delays with Earth can exceed 12 minutes, which can easily be the difference between life and death. By catching both subtle and significant deviations from standard daily fluctuations in various medical elements, space crews can be alerted to emerging risks early and take action.
details:
What the project does and how it works:

Put simply, it processes the telemetry of crew members on deep space missions, collecting a variety of physiological, environmental, and behavioural data to establish baselines for each astronaut. These baselines are calculated using mission days 1-14 of the space flight using direction-adjusted Z-scores and 3-day rolling averages to catch gradual drift. Furthermore, it pairs them with an Isolation Forest secondary score, and applies domain safeguards to ensure that shifts from the baseline are not treated immediately as anomalies, but taken in context.

The model translates amber or red statuses into non-technical explanations, using NASA HRP's risk areas as a guideline, that allow the crew to immediately understand the problem and either take onboard action or escalate to Earth. Live data is presented, via a FastAPI backend, in a React dashboard with offline fallback snapshots, allowing analysis across the mission duration, or across the entire crew at once.

Intended impact:

1. Autonomous Decision Support Under Communication Delays: Enablement of astronauts to identify, compounding, low-grade changes before they become critical.

2. Reduced Alert Fatigue: By calibrating to each astronaut's personal baseline and accounting for exercise context, the detector achieved 1.00 precision (0 false alarms across 176 normal synthetic days) while flagging gradual multi-signal fatigue and physiological drift.

3. Transparent, Non-Diagnostic Guidance: Every flags points to exact anomalous deviations and sources verified NASA/CSA links

Creativity and Key Design Factors Considered:

  • Compound Multi-Signal Detection Over Single-Threshold Alarms: Instead of waiting for one vital sign to hit an extreme emergency threshold, our approach highlights how three moderate, sub-clinical shifts (e.g., declining sleep, slower reaction time, and rising resting heart rate alongside elevated radiation) combine into an actionable amber pattern.
  • Contextual Safeguards & Communication Delay Awareness: We explicitly modeled domain edge cases—treating daily radiation as contextual risk rather than a standalone physiological trigger, suppressing false alarms on heavy exercise days, and separating onboard self-care actions from Earth-escalation protocols.
  • Scientific Integrity & Resilience: Because real continuous astronaut medical telemetry is restricted, we strictly separated synthetic ground-truth scenario labels from model inputs, documented all NASA/CSA research sources, framed all outputs as decision support rather than medical diagnosis, and built automatic JSON fallback snapshots so the dashboard functions reliably even without a live server connection.

Tools, Languages, and Software Used:

  • Languages: Python, JavaScript (JSX), HTML/CSS, PowerShell/Bash.
  • Data & Machine Learning: pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn (Isolation Forest, statistical Z-score & rolling drift modeling).
  • Backend & Testing: FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, Requests, pytest.
  • Frontend & Visualization: React, Vite, Recharts.
  • Collaboration & Architecture: Git/GitHub with feature-branch workflows, modular flat-file data contracts (CSV/JSON), and static fallback snapshot exporters.
